- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often overshoots early in forecast horizon; cap peak forecasts at 2–3 standard deviations above recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; apply a 1–2 day lagged mean reversion adjustment.
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish, model fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast slope by 15–20% in the first 3–5 days of sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early (first 5–7 days) and underpredicts late (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric smoothing: weight early days 0.4x, late days 0.6x.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” cycles (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model tends to misread momentum; use sentiment decay factor (e.g., 0.7 per 3-day shift) to dampen forecast volatility.
